source: Shu Qi, Technical Implementation Brief - Part 2 (Market Signal Scoring, Company Qualification & Intel Portfolio Mapping)
note: Version 1 values from the brief. Editable in the app (Settings); scores, tiers and qualification are recomputed from the stored evidence-backed ratings whenever these change.

rating_scale.label: Limited
rating_scale.meaning: Early indications, but insufficient supporting evidence.

rating_scale.label: Moderate
rating_scale.meaning: Credible evidence of activity, but incomplete or developing.

rating_scale.label: Strong
rating_scale.meaning: Clear and substantial evidence of relevant activity.

dimensions.label: Custom-silicon activity & strategic relevance
dimensions.evaluate: Proprietary silicon programmes, custom ASICs, processors, chiplet architectures and related development initiatives.

dimensions.label: Engineering capability & hiring momentum
dimensions.evaluate: Hiring activity, semiconductor engineering teams, chiplet architecture, RTL, physical design and packaging capabilities.

dimensions.label: Development maturity & progression
dimensions.evaluate: Prototypes, tape-outs, silicon validation, development milestones and progression towards deployment.

dimensions.label: External supplier & ecosystem signals
dimensions.evaluate: Foundry engagement, external IP licensing, packaging partnerships, supplier evaluations and manufacturing collaborations.

dimensions.label: Intel offering fit
dimensions.evaluate: Potential alignment with Intel Foundry, process technologies, design enablement, IP, advanced packaging, chiplet integration, assembly and test.

dimensions.label: Evidence strength & recency
dimensions.evaluate: Reliability, specificity, corroboration and recency of supporting evidence.

development_stages.label: Early Exploration
development_stages.criteria: Exploring chiplet architectures, custom silicon or related technologies, with limited evidence of active development.

development_stages.label: Capability Build
development_stages.criteria: Hiring semiconductor engineers, building internal silicon teams or establishing dedicated development capabilities.

development_stages.label: Active Development
development_stages.criteria: Actively developing proprietary silicon, custom ASICs, chiplet architectures or related technologies.

development_stages.label: External Ecosystem Engagement
development_stages.criteria: Engaging external foundries, IP providers, packaging partners or other semiconductor ecosystem participants.

development_stages.label: Supplier Evaluation / Commercial Engagement
development_stages.criteria: Evidence of supplier evaluation, manufacturing arrangements, design partnerships, packaging agreements or commercial engagement.

stage_rules.note: Do not assign a higher stage based on an isolated or unverified signal.

evidence_confidence.high: Direct primary-source evidence, such as company announcements, official hiring pages and confirmed partnerships.

questions.label: Custom-silicon relevance
questions.question: Does the company develop or commission proprietary/custom silicon?

questions.label: External semiconductor requirement
questions.question: Is there a plausible external requirement for semiconductor manufacturing, design/IP or advanced packaging?

questions.label: Intel portfolio alignment
questions.question: Is there a plausible fit with at least one area of Intel's portfolio?

outcomes.qualified: Passes Q1, Q2 and Q3 - eligible for Intel prospect shortlist.
outcomes.conditional: Q1 passes, but Q2 or Q3 requires further validation - retain for monitoring/investigation.
outcomes.not_qualified_q1: Fails Q1 - exclude from Module 1 prospect shortlist.
outcomes.not_qualified_fit: No plausible external requirement or Intel portfolio alignment - exclude from active prospect shortlist.

shortlist.note: Not determined by score alone: a company must be Qualified. Order by score/tier, development stage, evidence confidence, then Intel portfolio fit.
